# 2 Baruch Chapter 87 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Baruch's Letters
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 87:1 — final location — Mamre

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I-Baruch went-to-the-oak-tree of-Mamre, beneath-which Abraham, our-father, once-prayed-to-the-LORD" |
| LOGOS | "I, Baruch, went to the oak tree of Mamre, beneath which Abraham, our father, once prayed to the Lord" |
| PNEUMA | "I, Baruch, went to the oak tree of Mamre — the tree beneath which our father Abraham once prayed to the Lord" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. The relative clause structure ('beneath which') is standard biblical narrative grammar preserved by LOGOS; PNEUMA's insertion of a dash and repetition of 'the tree' is an editorial addition not in the Syriac.

---

## 87:1 — angels visiting Abraham

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "when-he-was-visited-by-his-angels" |
| LOGOS | "when he was visited by his angels" |
| PNEUMA | "when the angels visited him" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. 'Visited by his angels' (Syriac: kad ethpqad men mal'awhe) uses the passive voice, keeping God as the implicit agent who sends his angels; PNEUMA's active 'the angels visited him' slightly shifts the agency.
